references.text: The fire on the altar shall be kept burning and must not go out. The priest shall add wood to the fire every morning. This shows that the fire on the altar was to be maintained continuously.
Fire went out from the presence of the Lord and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. This demonstrates God's approval of the sacrificial service at the altar.
The sons of Aaron and their priestly service at the altar are described here, showing the priests' responsibility for the fire and the sacrificial service.
Elijah placed wood on the altar on Mount Carmel. This recalls the priests' practice of adding wood to the altar.
Fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering when Solomon's temple was dedicated, demonstrating God's acceptance of the altar and the offerings.
Ezekiel describes the dimensions of the altar where burnt offerings are to be made. This connects to the function of the altar in Leviticus.
Complementary descriptions of the ritual process: setting up the fire and wood (1:7) leads directly to burning the offering on this fire (3:5).
Theological basis and execution: Lev 6:2 commands that the altar's fire must burn forever, which gives meaning to the instruction to stack wood in Lev 1:7.
